intro: La Hacienda Estates is a small subdivision of lots and homes near the La Hacienda and Hudson Bend Road area. CleanzATX covers it as part of our Hudson Bend route, and Tyler Durham answers every request himself.

sections.h2: What La Hacienda Estates homes are like
paragraphs: La Hacienda Estates is a small neighborhood on the Hudson Bend peninsula. It has both finished homes and open lots, with prices that run from about $400K up to $1M. It has no gate, and the listing record shows no HOA, so owners generally handle exterior upkeep themselves.

Because the area is mixed and still developing, you can see older homes beside newer ones on nearby lots. That variety is common around Hudson Bend, and it helps to remember when you ask for a quote, since the age and size of each house shape the work.

sections.h2: What La Hacienda Estates windows deal with
paragraphs: Being on the peninsula means the lake is never far. Hard water in the air and from sprinklers leaves white spots on glass, and in time those spots can etch. Wind and dust from Hudson Bend Road, open lots and nearby building work add a layer of grit, so windows here get dirty in a way that a quick rinse does not fix.

Older homes tend to have wood or aluminum frames with a lot of build up in the tracks. Spider webs and leaf litter also collect in the corners of screens. Track cleaning is $5, screens are $5, and hard water spot removal is $10 per pane.

sections.h2: How we work La Hacienda Estates
paragraphs: We treat La Hacienda Estates as one stop in a Hudson Bend day. That keeps the cost low for you, since we are already close by. We bring our own pure water, so there is no need to leave a hose on, and we work from the ground with water fed poles. If the home has a pool deck or patio, we can clean it by hand later, so it does not get soaked.
For a 2,000 sq ft home, exterior windows come to about $200 at $0.10 per sq ft, which is also our minimum job. Expect about one and a half to two hours on site for the outside.
